ONE SUITE REACHES ONE SOURCE FILE: tools/mutate.py takes a single `source` from suites.json -- the manifest loader refuses an entry that is not exactly [source, binary] and the runner reads that one file -- so the other three members of V90Modem::progress's closure (V90BitsToSymbol::process(unsigned char *, unsigned int &, short *), V90Modem::progress and V90Phase4Modulator::generateSymbol) live in three other files and would each need a suite of their own pointed at this same binary, which is what t_v90modchain already has five of.  All three are DRIVEN by t_v90modprog and counted in its denominators; they are simply not mutated here.  ONE ROW IS UNCAUGHT AND IT IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO THE TOOL.  `the phase 3 arm copies the event code even when it is zero` deletes the `if (phase3Modulator->eventCode != 0)` guard, and no trial can currently see it: the guard only matters when a NON-ZERO event arrives and a later symbol of the SAME block reports zero, and the only phase 3 event this fixture can produce is 6 -- which moves `state` to 2, so every symbol after it goes to the phase 4 arm and its own guard.  Reaching it needs V90Phase3Modulator driven to a TRN1d, Jd or JdPhase boundary (eventCode 1, 2 and 3 at src/pump/v90/V90Phase3Modulator.cpp lines 436, 451 and 621), which is a different poke from the DIL cursors `p3fire` sets.  It is NOT declared equivalent: the guard is observable in principle, so the gap is in the sweep and not in the arithmetic.

NOT here: making V90Modulator::state unsigned.  That is a change to include/dsplib/V90Modulator.h and not to this file, and the object's `cmp $0x1 ; je ; jle` at 0x1a848 is the whole evidence for the signedness -- a behavioural test sees it only through a negative state, which t_v90modprog drives, and a mutation of the DECLARATION belongs to whichever suite owns that header.
